Empirical Research Plan:  “Pension‐Contribution Shocks and Corporate Investment”

-------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-------------------------------------------------
Chosen method:  Regression Discontinuity in an Instrumental-Variables (RD-IV) framework (“fuzzy” RD).

Why it fits

• Institutional kink/discontinuity – The statutory funding rule sets mandated pension contributions equal to zero when the plan’s funding status crosses 100 %.  
• Exogenous variation – Annual funding status is driven largely by market returns and interest-rate movements that are orthogonal to a firm’s concurrent investment opportunities.  
• Objective – We need the causal effect of exogenous cash drains (mandatory contributions) on investment.  The discontinuity gives us an instrument for contributions; a local Wald estimator delivers the causal impact on investment for firms close to the cutoff.

The design therefore combines the transparency of RD (credibility, graphical diagnostics) with the ability to scale the shock by means of a first-stage (IV).

-------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-------------------------------------------------
Running variable  
FS_it ≡ Pension assets_it – ABO liabilities_it, scaled by ABO liabilities (so 0 = exact 100 % funding).

Cutoff  
c = 0.

Sharpness  
Fuzzy: E[Mand. Contrib_it | FS_it < 0] > E[Mand. Contrib_it | FS_it ≥ 0].

Treatment indicator  
T_it = 1{FS_it < 0}.  It instruments the continuous treatment,  
MC_it = Mandatory pension contribution / Lagged assets.

Control group  
Firms with 0 %–h % overfunding (FS in [0,h]).  

Treatment group  
Firms with 0 %–h % underfunding (FS in [–h,0)).  Main bandwidth h chosen via Calonico–Cattaneo–Titiunik MSE selector.

Event date  
Fiscal year t: Funding status measured at the beginning of the fiscal year; mandatory contribution is legally due within that fiscal year; investment outcomes (CapEx, R&D, acquisitions) are measured over the same fiscal year.  This timing avoids reverse-causality.

Extension/robustness  
Additional statutory kinks at 90 % and 80 % funding generate separate cutoffs to replicate the analysis.

-------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-------------------------------------------------
A1. No precise manipulation of funding status around 0.  
Plausibility: Funding status depends mainly on exogenous market returns; sponsors cannot instantaneously revalue assets to jump the cutoff.  We will formally test for bunching (McCrary density test).

A2. Continuity of potential outcomes at FS = 0 in absence of treatment.  
Plausible because nothing other than mandatory contributions changes discretely at the 100 % threshold.

A3. Exclusion restriction for IV: Crossing the cutoff affects investment only through the cash obligation, not via other channels.  
Reasonable given the institutional detail; we will check for discontinuities in non-cash variables such as Tobin’s Q or growth opportunities.

A4. Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers within the bandwidth).  
Within-firm shocks do not directly change other firms’ FS; equilibrium spillovers are addressed in §6 with a separate general-equilibrium test.

-------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
-------------------------------------------------
T1. Strategic smoothing of funding status (sponsor contributions, asset reallocation).  
Mitigation: Density test; placebo RD on lagged FS; restrict bandwidth to narrow window (e.g. ±5 %).  Results robust to dropping observations with quarter-end asset transfers flagged in 10-Ks.

T2. Funding status may proxy for latent firm health, violating continuity.  
Mitigation: Show covariate balance (size, Q, leverage, prior CapEx) on both sides of cutoff; include these controls in the RD-IV; show flat pre-trend graphs.

T3. Timing mismatch (investment could occur before the cash shock is felt).  
Mitigation: Use contribution rules that are set at plan-year start; investment is measured over the same fiscal year; alternatively run lagged-outcome regressions as placebo (should be zero).

-------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-------------------------------------------------
```r
#----------------------------------------------------
# 0. Libraries
#----------------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)      # fast high-dimensional FE
library(rdrobust)    # RD estimation
library(AER)         # IV estimation
#----------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and merge data
#----------------------------------------------------
comp <- read_csv("compustat_db_firmyear_1990_1998.csv")      # firm-level vars
pen  <- read_csv("irs5500_planlevel_1990_1998.csv")          # pension vars

df <- comp %>%
      left_join(pen, by = c("gvkey","fyear")) %>%
      filter(!is.na(plan_assets) & !is.na(plan_liab)) %>%
      arrange(gvkey, fyear)

#----------------------------------------------------
# 2. Variable construction
#----------------------------------------------------
df <- df %>%
  mutate(fs          = (plan_assets - plan_liab) / plan_liab,         # funding status
         treat       = ifelse(fs < 0, 1, 0),
         mc          = mand_contrib / lag(total_assets),
         capex       = capx / lag(total_assets),
         r_and_d     = xrd / lag(total_assets),
         acqu        = acquisitions / lag(total_assets),
         cashflow    = oancf / lag(total_assets),
         q           = tobinq,                                         # provided
         window      = abs(fs) <= 0.05)                               # 5 % bandwidth

#----------------------------------------------------
# 3. Local polynomial RD-IV (within selected window)
#----------------------------------------------------
rd_data  <- df %>% filter(window)

# First-stage
first <- feols(mc ~ fs + treat | gvkey + fyear, data = rd_data, cluster = ~gvkey)
summary(first)

# Second-stage IV using treat as instrument (local Wald)
iv_main <- feols(capex ~ 1 | gvkey + fyear | (mc ~ treat), data = rd_data,
                 cluster = ~gvkey)
summary(iv_main)

# rdrobust check (automatic bandwidth)
rd_out <- rdrobust(y = rd_data$capex, x = rd_data$fs, fuzzy = rd_data$treat)
summary(rd_out)

#----------------------------------------------------
# 4. Heterogeneity by financial constraints (KZ quintile)
#----------------------------------------------------
rd_data <- rd_data %>%
           mutate(kz_high = ifelse(kz_index > median(kz_index, na.rm = TRUE), 1, 0))

iv_het <- feols(capex ~ kz_high | gvkey + fyear | (mc ~ treat*kz_high),
                data = rd_data, cluster = ~gvkey)
summary(iv_het)

#----------------------------------------------------
# 5. Robustness: placebo cutoff at +7 %
#----------------------------------------------------
df <- df %>%
      mutate(treat_pbo = ifelse(fs < 0.07 & fs >= 0.02, 1, 0),
             window_pb = fs >= 0.02 & fs <= 0.12)

pb_data <- df %>% filter(window_pb)

pb_iv <- feols(capex ~ 1 | gvkey + fyear | (mc ~ treat_pbo),
               data = pb_data, cluster = ~gvkey)
summary(pb_iv)
```

-------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-------------------------------------------------
Economic prior:  A forced $1 of pension contribution lowers contemporaneous CapEx by roughly $0.25–$0.40 for financially constrained firms; little or no effect for unconstrained firms.  R&D—being more footloose—may fall by ~$0.15/$1.  We expect acquisitions to drop the most (lumpy, easily postponed).  In the equilibrium test, non-DB firms’ investment should rise modestly (≈ +$0.05/$1).

-------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RD)
-------------------------------------------------
C1: No sorting around cutoff ………………………………… 1  
C2: Covariate balance/continuity ………………………… 1  
C3: Correct bandwidth & functional form …………… 1  
C4: No simultaneous policy changes at cutoff …… 0.5 (small, but need to rule out PBGC premia)  
C5: Robustness & placebo checks  ……………………… 1  

Overall credibility score: 4.5 / 5.

-------------------------------------------------
End of plan
